snapshotNote: Snapshot 05:37 UTC · waivers clear 07:00 UTC (01:00 Wednesday, Mexico City) — about 65 minutes from this file. This run fired at 05:41 UTC, roughly seven hours before its usual 13:00 UTC slot, so unlike every other Wednesday brief it lands BEFORE the claims process rather than after. If you are reading this at breakfast, the window has shut and the post-waiver half of each card is the part that still applies. This brief does not refresh on its own.
sources: Built from 19 searches and 17 page reads · FantasyPros, Sportsnaut, FantasyLife, Pro Football Network, DraftKings Network, NBC Sports/Rotoworld, RotoWire, Sports Illustrated/On SI, Yahoo Sports, Squawka, Draft Sharks, ESPN league file

tonight.headline: Three claims, about an hour. One of them changed since the last brief — take Tampa Bay, not Baltimore.
body: Week 2 has not kicked off. On this 05:37 snapshot ESPN has Panda Attack 124.8 to your 123.0 and gives you 49%. Nothing is locked and your lineup is already the one this brief agrees with — no starter change is recommended in Chem this run.

Everything live is the waiver run at 07:00 UTC. One card moved since the 04:30 brief, and it is a genuine upgrade rather than a reversal: the defense you should claim is Tampa Bay, not Baltimore. Tampa is 1st on FantasyPros' Week 2 board and the outright top recommendation on FantasyLife's streamer column, at 13.1% rostered here against Baltimore's 89.8%. Baltimore was never wrong; Tampa is simply the better instance of the same argument, and four managers ahead of you in priority are far likelier to be sitting on the 89.8% name.

case.label: Why Tampa Bay is the better claim
case.body: Jacksonville's defense earned its Week 1 reputation by sacking Deshaun Watson five times. Tampa Bay play Cleveland this week — they inherit the exact matchup that produced those numbers. FantasyLife, 15 September: Watson 'took five sacks and threw one interception with several other close calls' and 'looked just as bad as the last time we saw him starting for the Browns.' Tampa are home and 8.5-point favourites. FantasyPros rank them 1st of 32 and Jacksonville 30th, with the stated reason that Jacksonville's five sacks 'came against Cleveland and I don't expect either of those things to repeat this week.' The correct response to that sentence is not to buy Baltimore. It is to buy whoever draws Cleveland.

case.label: The dissent, stated
case.body: Sportsnaut's Week 2 board disagrees on the incumbent: it has Jacksonville 8th and Tampa Bay 4th, so on that board the upgrade is two places rather than twenty-nine. I take FantasyPros on Jacksonville for the same reason as the last brief — Sportsnaut's Jacksonville note is a description of the Cleveland box score, and FantasyPros is the board arguing about what happens next. Both boards agree Tampa Bay is top five, so the claim itself does not depend on resolving that fight.

case.label: Order matters more than usual
case.body: This is priority waivers, not FAAB. Winning a claim drops you to the back of the order for the rest of the same run, so your three claims are not independent — the first one you win is the one you are most likely to get. That is the entire reason these are numbered. Coker first because he is the only one of the three who could start for you; Tampa second; Loop third because a kicker is worth roughly a point and a half.

case.label: What decides your matchup
case.body: Panda Attack reset their lineup at 15:25 Monday and start Dak Prescott with Jalen Hurts benched — a 20-point quarterback either way in a one-QB league. They carry Davante Adams, Jaylen Waddle and Dalton Kincaid. Jordan Mason sits on their bench with a thumb that DraftKings on 15 September still lists as 'being evaluated' after soreness in the Green Bay win. Their problem, not yours, and it is why their projected total is soft.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: A manager ahead of you in priority takes Tampa Bay at 07:00, in which case Baltimore at 89.8% rostered is the fallback and is still 3rd on the FantasyPros board. Priority resets weekly in Chem, so a failed claim costs you nothing at all and there is no version of tonight where placing all three is wrong.

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 07:00 UTC · place this claim FIRST
doFirst.title: Claim Jalen Coker, drop Matthew Stafford
doFirst.subtitle: Unchanged and now better sourced. DraftKings' 15 September report has him expected to play and calls the ankle minor — newer than anything the last brief had.

case.label: What is new since 04:30
case.body: The last brief said plainly that nothing had landed on the ankle since 14 September and that you were claiming blind. That is no longer true. DraftKings Network's Week 2 injury report, dated 15 September, lists Coker under Ankle with status 'Expected to play Sunday', notes he was hurt 'rolling his ankle in the first quarter at Chicago', that 'Coker called the injury minor', and that he led Carolina in receiving in Week 1. The blind claim is now a sighted one.

case.label: The role
case.body: 8 catches on 9 targets for 138 yards and two touchdowns in Week 1 — the best receiver line of the week and a career high in yardage. The Charlotte Observer's framing on 14 September: 'Tetairoa McMillan is Carolina's No. 1 receiver. Jalen Coker is playing like one.' Over Carolina's last two games Coker has out-produced McMillan, who managed 5 for 75 and a fumble in Week 1.

case.label: The anomaly
case.body: 51.1% rostered with ownership rising — +0.34 on this snapshot, one of only two positive movers in the wire's entire receiver band. A WR30 sitting free in a ten-team league is a manager blunder, not a verdict on the player. That is the OWNED signal and it is the strongest thing a waiver wire can hold.

case.label: A trap that nearly landed here
case.body: A CBS Sports item titled 'Panthers' Jalen Coker: Logs full practice' surfaces at the top of search for this player. It is dated 8 October 2025 and describes a quadriceps injury from a different season. It is not evidence about this ankle and it was not used. Flagging it because it is the single most misleading result a search on this name returns.

case.label: The drop
case.body: Matthew Stafford is your second quarterback in a league that starts one. He has not been startable behind Josh Allen for a single week and will not be. Dropping him also retires the JuiceJam offer below — accepted on purpose, and the trade card explains why that costs you nothing real.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Carolina's Wednesday report has him limited or not practising, or he carries a designation into Sunday; or McMillan reasserts as the clear alpha and Coker's target share falls under about 18% across Weeks 2–3. Either says the claim was the wrong kind of brave.

doFirst.sources: DraftKings Network · Charlotte Observer · NBC Sports · Yahoo Sports · ESPN league file

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 07:00 UTC · place this claim SECOND
doFirst.title: Claim the Buccaneers defense, drop the Jaguars defense
doFirst.subtitle: Changed since the last brief. Tampa Bay, not Baltimore — 1st on one board, 4th on the other, and rostered by almost nobody.

case.label: The upgrade over the last brief
case.body: The 04:30 card said claim Baltimore. The reasoning was right and the name was not the best available. FantasyPros' Week 2 board has Tampa Bay 1st — 'a high-end target for fantasy defenses' with Watson starting — and Baltimore 3rd. FantasyLife's streamer column on 15 September leads with Tampa Bay outright ahead of Green Bay and Kansas City. Sportsnaut has Tampa 4th and Baltimore 6th. Every board retrieved this run puts Tampa above Baltimore.

case.label: The argument in one line
case.body: Your Jacksonville defense scored its Week 1 points against Deshaun Watson. Tampa Bay get Watson this week. Rather than paying for Jacksonville's reputation, claim the team holding the fixture that built it.

case.label: Why it is also the cheaper claim
case.body: Tampa Bay is 13.1% rostered here and 3% nationally per FantasyLife; Baltimore is 89.8%. Four managers sit ahead of you in priority. If any of them is streaming a defense tonight, they are looking at the 89.8% name, not the 13% one. Claiming Tampa is both the better unit and the likelier one to actually land.

case.label: The honest size
case.body: ESPN's own weekly numbers make this 8.5 against 5.5 — three points, the largest single-position gap on your roster this week, but defense scoring is high-variance and one week of board consensus is doing most of the work. The claim is free in Chem, which is the rest of the argument. Tampa are home and 8.5-point favourites, which is the scoring environment you want behind a defense.

case.label: The churn objection, answered
case.body: This seat has now been discussed three times in three days — blocked, then Baltimore, now Tampa Bay. That is a fair thing to be suspicious of. The distinction: the reasoning never moved, only the name. All three readings agreed Jacksonville should go; the disagreement was about what replaces it, and Tampa Bay was available the whole time and went unnamed. That is an omission being corrected, not a thesis being flipped.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Tampa Bay finish outside the top 12 defense scores in Week 2, or Jacksonville finish top 5 at Denver. Either says two boards were reading one game and this seat got churned for nothing.

action.label: Claim Buccaneers D/ST · drop Jaguars D/ST

doFirst.deadlineLabel: Waivers clear 07:00 UTC · place this claim THIRD
doFirst.title: Claim Tyler Loop, drop Chris Boswell
doFirst.subtitle: K4 against K17 on this week's board, confirmed again this run. Third because a kicker is worth about a point and a half, not because the case weakened.

case.label: The board, re-retrieved
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 kicker rankings, 14 September, read in full this run: Aubrey 1, Dicker 2, Cam Little 3, Tyler Loop 4, Reichard 5, McLaughlin 6, Bates 7, Bass 8, Myers 9, Elliott 10, Fairbairn 11, Pineiro 12, Smack 13, Santos 14, McPherson 15 — and Chris Boswell 17. Loop's entry carries reasoning: 'If the Ravens continue moving the ball at anything close to their Week 1 rate, Loop should have enough field-goal and extra-point chances to justify his K4 ranking.' Boswell's entry carries none.

case.label: The draw
case.body: Baltimore host New Orleans, who surrendered five first-half sacks in Week 1 while Tyler Shough threw for 410 in a game that stayed open. Boswell travels to New England, 5th on Sportsnaut's Week 2 defense board. Kicker scoring follows the offense's scoring environment and these two point opposite ways.

case.label: The honest size
case.body: ESPN's weekly numbers put this at 8.6 against 7.4 — under a point and a half. The thirteen-place ranking gap is the argument; the projection is not. It clears the bar only because it is free, which is also why it is placed third.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: Boswell finishes top 10 among kickers in Week 2 while Loop finishes outside the top 20, or Baltimore's implied team total falls below 22 for two straight weeks.

whatWentWrong.title: The last brief told you to claim Baltimore. Tampa Bay was sitting on the same wire, ranked higher on every board, and went unnamed.
whatWentWrong.lead: Not a reversal of reasoning — an omission. The argument for dropping Jacksonville was correct at 04:30 and is correct now. The replacement was the second-best one available.

case.label: What the last brief said
case.body: It moved the Baltimore card back to SOLID and into second place on the strength of FantasyPros having Baltimore 3rd and Jacksonville 30th. Both numbers were right. What it did not do was read down to 1st on the board it was quoting.

case.label: What was missed
case.body: Tampa Bay is 1st on that same FantasyPros board and the lead recommendation in FantasyLife's 15 September streamer column, at 3% rostered nationally and 13.1% here. It is also the team that draws Cleveland — the fixture that generated Jacksonville's Week 1 sack total in the first place. The board being quoted contained the better answer two rows above the one that was taken.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: The claim is now Tampa Bay, still second in the queue. Baltimore becomes the explicit fallback if a rival takes Tampa. Nothing has been lost because no claim has processed — but if you already queued Baltimore, change it, and if you cannot, Baltimore is still a clear upgrade on Jacksonville.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Tampa Bay finish outside the top 12 in Week 2 while Baltimore finish top 5. Then the 89.8%-rostered name was the market being right and the ownership anomaly was noise.

whatWentWrong.sources: FantasyPros · FantasyLife · Sportsnaut · ESPN league file

whatWentWrong.title: The Coker claim was described as blind. It no longer is, and the reason is a report that existed before the last brief was written.
whatWentWrong.lead: DraftKings Network published a Week 2 injury round-up on 15 September carrying Coker as expected to play. The 04:30 brief said nothing had landed since 14 September.

case.label: What was said
case.body: 'Nothing new landed on Coker in the six hours since the last brief, and that is the finding.' It went on to accept a blind claim on the grounds that priority is free in Chem. The conclusion was right. The premise was not.

case.label: What existed
case.body: DraftKings Network's Week 2 injury report, 15 September, lists Coker with status 'Expected to play Sunday', the injury described by the player as minor, and a note that he led Carolina in receiving in Week 1. Same publisher as one of the sources already cited on the card, one day newer, and not retrieved.

case.label: What it changes
case.body: Nothing about the action — the claim was already first in the queue. It changes the confidence, and it removes 'you are claiming blind' from the card. Worth logging because the failure mode was searching the player's name rather than the week's aggregated report.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Carolina's Wednesday practice report contradicts the DraftKings line. That report lands after 07:00 either way, which is the structural problem no amount of searching fixes.

roster.footnote: Nothing has kicked off. Josh Allen locks first, Thursday 18:15 Mexico City; Likely and Stafford are Monday night. Grades are matchup grades from the offence's point of view — GREAT means a good place to start your guy. Every tile is graded from a Week 2 board retrieved this run, named in the evidence line; read the grade note in Blind spots before trusting them, because two weeks in there is no season sample underneath them.

starting.name: Josh Allen
starting.detail: BUF · vs DET · Thu 18:15 · locks first of anyone you own. No change recommended.
starting.gradeEvidence: Detroit outside the top 20 on Sportsnaut's Week 2 board — a bound, not a rank

starting.name: De'Von Achane
starting.detail: MIA · @ SF · Sun 14:25 · Malik Willis is throwing, not Tagovailoa. Willis went 15-of-27 and was sacked five times in Week 1; Achane ran 11 times for 36 yards, 3.3 a carry. Squawka's model has San Francisco by 8 with a 30-13 scoreline. The counter-argument, and it is real in full PPR: a two-score deficit is the game script that turns him into a receiver.
starting.gradeEvidence: San Francisco 2nd on Sportsnaut's Week 2 board; Miami implied around 13 points

starting.name: Jaylen Warren
starting.detail: PIT · @ NE · Sun 11:00 · Aaron Rodgers throwing. Carried from the last brief and not re-verified this run: CBS had him pegged preseason for 'the bulk of the pass-catching work' and he delivered 5 catches on 6 targets in Week 1. In full PPR that receiving role is most of his floor.
starting.gradeEvidence: New England 5th on Sportsnaut's Week 2 board

starting.name: Terry McLaurin
starting.detail: WSH · @ DAL · Sun 14:25 · Jayden Daniels throwing, confirmed for Week 2. Contested: he ran 92.1% of Washington's routes in Week 1, highest on the team, and caught 2 for 14. Yahoo's 15 September preview says outright he 'looks like he's lost a step'. Usage says hold, efficiency says sell, and this brief holds — but it is no longer a one-sided read.

starting.name: Justin Jefferson
starting.detail: MIN · @ CHI · Sun 11:00 · Carson Wentz throwing, not Kyler Murray, who is in concussion protocol and evaluated daily. That is good news, not bad: Jefferson went 8-92-2 for 27.2 points with Wentz in relief in Week 1, his highest single-game total since 2024. One caveat on sourcing — DraftKings' round-up says Cam Ward finished that game, which is wrong; Ward is Tennessee's quarterback in this same file. SI and the Star Tribune both say Wentz, and the league file has Wentz on Minnesota.
starting.gradeEvidence: Chicago 30th on Sportsnaut's Week 2 board — the softest draw on your roster

starting.name: Garrett Wilson
starting.detail: NYJ · vs GB · Sun 11:00 · Geno Smith throwing. He worked as a game manager in Week 1 — 9.0 yards per attempt, zero sacks taken — and Wilson still led the Jets in receiving yards. Low attempt volume is the risk; the efficiency and the target share are not.
starting.gradeEvidence: Green Bay 16th on Sportsnaut's board, 9th on FantasyPros' — the two disagree, so this tile is the midpoint

starting.name: Isaiah Likely
starting.detail: NYG · @ LAR · Mon 18:15 · Jaxson Dart throwing, and the connection is real — Dart's first touchdown pass of 2026 was a 15-yard loft to Likely. Carried from the last brief: 8 targets, second only to Nabers, 22 routes to Theo Johnson's 14. He is the undisputed starter at the position.
starting.gradeEvidence: Los Angeles Rams 9th on Sportsnaut's Week 2 board

starting.detail: JAX · @ DEN · Sun 14:05 · the Tampa Bay claim above replaces this. Roster share fell 0.82 on this snapshot, the sharpest move anywhere in your wire. Its five Week 1 sacks came against Cleveland, and Cleveland is now Tampa Bay's fixture.
starting.gradeEvidence: 30th on FantasyPros' Week 2 board; 8th on Sportsnaut's, and this brief takes FantasyPros

starting.name: Chris Boswell
starting.detail: PIT · @ NE · Sun 11:00 · K17 on Pro Football Network's Week 2 board with no analysis attached, against Loop at K4 with a stated reason. The Loop claim above replaces him if it lands.

bench.name: Kyle Pitts Sr.
bench.detail: ATL · vs CAR · Sun 11:00 · still no named quarterback, and nothing published since 14 September resolves it. Carried: he ran a route on 81% of dropbacks in Week 1, tied 7th among tight ends. Hold on the role; he is not startable over Likely while Atlanta cannot name a passer.

bench.name: Brian Thomas Jr.
bench.detail: JAX · @ DEN · Sun 14:05 · Lawrence throwing. DraftKings, 15 September: shoulder, 'briefly left Sunday's win over the Browns before returning', limited in practice, coach expects him available. The uncomfortable number carried forward — 14 routes in Week 1 to Jakobi Meyers's 20. Jacksonville's implied total at Denver is about 20.

bench.name: Bhayshul Tuten
bench.detail: JAX · @ DEN · Sun 14:05 · the case for benching him is now specific. Draft Sharks on his Week 1 usage: Chris Rodriguez 'took the only goal-line snap and five of the team's eight short-yardage plays', and Tuten 'actually ran two fewer pass routes' than Rodriguez despite playing five more snaps. A back who owns neither the goal line nor passing downs is capped, and in full PPR that costs twice. Denver missing 28 tackles against Kansas City is the case for him if there is one.

bench.name: Kyle Monangai
bench.detail: CHI · vs MIN · Sun 11:00 · Caleb Williams throwing, and Chicago scored 59 points in Week 1. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4, which is why the 13 September recommendation to drop him stays logged as wrong. Not startable over Warren this week, but do not drop him for a kicker or a defense.

bench.name: Matthew Stafford
bench.detail: LAR · vs NYG · Mon 18:15 · the drop on the Coker claim. Your second quarterback in a one-QB league; he has not been startable behind Allen once this season. If the Coker claim fails, he stays and nothing is lost.
bench.gradeEvidence: New York Giants not retrieved on any board this run — the last brief had them 14th on Sportsnaut's, carried but unverified

trades.theirGainLine: Their gain is +3.8 on season projections — real but thin, which is most of why three sends went unanswered.

case.label: Recomputed on this snapshot, unchanged
case.body: Re-run against the 05:37 file on that league's own slot rules: +21.8 you, +3.8 them on season projections — identical to the last five snapshots. It stays on the screen because the previous run's work is not deleted by a new run starting. It is still not recommended and should not be re-sent.

case.label: The weekly maths actually fails
case.body: Priced on this week's projections instead of season, their side comes out at minus 0.1 — it does not clear the both-sides-gain test at all. The entire +3.8 lives in a season field that has not moved in five snapshots. Two units, two answers, and the one that says yes is the one built on a preseason artifact.

case.label: Why it stopped being recommended
case.body: It was built on McLaurin being in decline. Week 1 usage says otherwise: 92.1% route participation, highest on Washington. Yahoo's 15 September preview takes the other side and says he has lost a step. Selling him at four targets is selling usage at its floor, and the honest position is that this is now genuinely contested rather than clearly wrong.

case.label: The slot column, checked
case.body: DeVonta Smith is JuiceJam's slot-4 starting receiver, not a bench piece — so this asks for a starter, which is part of why three sends went unanswered. DJ Moore at 209.0 sits on their bench and would backfill. Their +3.8 comes almost entirely from Stafford replacing Jared Goff at quarterback, 303.4 against 277.8, and a real manager looking at Goff's Week 1 is unlikely to see it the way the arithmetic does.

case.label: The clock
case.body: This offer dies at 07:00 if the Coker claim is awarded, because Stafford is the drop. Accepted, not overlooked: a claim on the week's best available receiver outranks an offer that has been declined three times and that this brief no longer recommends.

case.label: Falsified if
case.body: McLaurin draws fewer than six targets at Dallas against a secondary missing Hooker and Overshown, or his route share drops below 80% across Weeks 2–3 while Diggs's climbs above it. Then the Week 1 route count was the anomaly and the sale should be reopened — with Stafford already spent on Coker.

trades.sources: ESPN league file · Yahoo Sports · Sports Illustrated/On SI · Draft Sharks
trades.copyText: Hey — long shot, but: McLaurin + Stafford for DeVonta Smith? You'd be consolidating two starters into one better one and you're carrying a quarterback you can't start. Straight up, no hard feelings if it's a no.

worthALook.name: Ravens D/ST
worthALook.lead: The fallback if a rival takes Tampa Bay at 07:00. 3rd on the FantasyPros board and still a large upgrade on what you own.

case.label: The case
case.body: FantasyPros Week 2, 15 September: Baltimore 3rd — 'The Ravens sacked Daniel Jones twice on 17 pressures last week, and I expect to see more of that pressure get home against the Saints.' Sportsnaut has them 6th. New Orleans gave up five first-half sacks in Week 1. Your incumbent is 30th on the same FantasyPros board.

case.label: Why it is second choice
case.body: Tampa Bay outranks Baltimore on all three boards retrieved this run and is rostered at 13.1% against Baltimore's 89.8%. The ownership gap is the practical point: the managers above you in priority are far more likely to be queueing the 89.8% name. Claiming Tampa is both the better unit and the less contested one.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Only if Tampa Bay is gone. Both are free claims in Chem, so if you can only place one defense claim, place Tampa — and if the 07:00 run has already passed by the time you read this, check whether either cleared unclaimed and add for nothing.

worthALook.sources: FantasyPros · Sportsnaut · FantasyLife · ESPN league file

worthALook.name: Jakobi Meyers
worthALook.lead: A listed starting receiver at 79% rostered — and he ran more Week 1 routes than the Jacksonville receiver you already own.

case.label: The role
case.body: Jacksonville publish three first-string receivers by alignment — Parker Washington in the slot, Brian Thomas Jr. on the left with Travis Hunter second, Meyers on the right. Different jobs rather than a WR1/2/3 ranking. Travis Hunter is a starting cornerback taking a package on offence, so there is no fourth mouth in that room.

case.label: The number that argues for him
case.body: Carried from 15 September NBC coverage and not re-verified tonight: Meyers ran 20 routes to Brian Thomas Jr.'s 14, the most of any Jacksonville receiver. It is the strongest fact on this page and it cuts against a player you own, which is why it stays written down.

case.label: The awkward part
case.body: He is the direct competitor to Brian Thomas Jr., and one of the falsification conditions on the Thomas thesis is literally 'Meyers out-targets him in Week 2'. Claiming both sides of that question is paying twice. Jacksonville's implied total at Denver is about 20, so you would also be stacking two receivers from a low-scoring projection.

case.label: When to act
case.body: Meyers out-targets Thomas at Denver, or Jacksonville rule Thomas out. Either turns this from a row into a claim — and by then it is a swap rather than a stack.

worthALook.sources: NBC Sports (carried from 15 Sep) · Sports Illustrated betting · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Stefon Diggs
doNotChase.lead: You cut him on 12 September. Re-adding him four days later is the reversal pattern this log exists to stop.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: 65.8% route participation in Week 1 against McLaurin's 92.1%. He is the second receiver in an offence whose coordinator has said out loud it is built to get McLaurin ten targets a game. You would be claiming the player whose usage lost the comparison.

case.label: The new wrinkle, stated honestly
case.body: Yahoo's 15 September Week 2 preview says Diggs 'still has something left in the tank' and names rookie Antonio Williams as an emerging target — which cuts against McLaurin more than it argues for Diggs. It is a reason to watch the Washington receiver room, not a reason to spend a roster seat on the second man in it.

case.label: The other cost
case.body: The only plausible drop is Brian Thomas Jr., who arrived the same day Diggs left. Rotating one seat through three players in a week is churn wearing a suit.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: McLaurin's route share falls under 80% across Weeks 2–3 while Diggs climbs above it, and Thomas is ruled out for a multi-week stretch. Both, not either.

doNotChase.sources: Yahoo Sports · Draft Sharks · ESPN league file

doNotChase.name: Eddy Pineiro
doNotChase.lead: The highest-owned kicker on this wire is K12 this week. If you place one kicker claim it should not be him.

case.label: The number that kills it
case.body: Pro Football Network's Week 2 board, read in full this run, has Pineiro 12th and Loop 4th. His season-long analyst rank is better than Loop's, which is exactly the trap: the season field is a preseason opinion, the weekly board is this week's draw.

case.label: The draw
case.body: San Francisco host Miami as roughly 8-to-13-point favourites in a game Squawka models 30-13. That is excellent for the 49ers defense, 2nd on Sportsnaut's board, and mediocre for a kicker who scores when drives stall in range rather than end in touchdowns.

case.label: What would change it
case.body: Loop misses twice from inside 45, or Baltimore's implied total falls below 22 for two straight weeks. Then the kicker seat reopens and Pineiro's ownership was telling you something after all.

settled.title: Start Terry McLaurin in the flex over Bhayshul Tuten (15 September)
settled.result: Executed 17:58 Monday and reaffirmed — 12.7 against 9.4. Strengthened this run from the other side: Draft Sharks show Tuten lost the goal line and the passing-down work to Chris Rodriguez in Week 1, so the gap is about role, not just projection.

settled.title: Start Isaiah Likely over Kyle Pitts (14 September)
settled.result: Executed 07:17 on 15 September. Confirmed again: Dart's first touchdown pass of 2026 went to Likely, and Atlanta still have no named quarterback for Pitts.

settled.title: Add Isaiah Likely (13 September)
settled.result: 27.8 with two touchdowns. Pattern note kept: the add landed two hours after Pitts's kickoff, so he could not have been started in Week 1. A Sunday-evening add costs a whole week, not a lineup slot.

settled.title: Add Brian Thomas Jr. for Stefon Diggs (12 September)
settled.result: Holding. Thomas's shoulder resolved to 'expected to play' on DraftKings' 15 September report. The route count against Meyers, 14 to 20, remains the open question on him.

settled.title: Start Jaylen Warren over Bhayshul Tuten (13 September)
settled.result: Reaffirmed. Warren's pass-catching role is the floor; Tuten's Week 1 usage shows him behind Rodriguez on both short yardage and routes.

settled.title: Drop Kyle Monangai for Tre Tucker (13 September)
settled.result: Still logged wrong. Monangai returned from the knee and scored 20.4 in Week 1. He is not startable over Warren, but he was never the drop.

settled.title: Block the Loop claim on a churn rule from the other league (15 September morning)
settled.result: Correctly overturned. That seven-day kicker rule came from IPADE's activity log, not Chem's. Chem shows no kicker transaction since the feed begins on 9 September.

cannotSee.label: This run fired seven hours early, and that is why it is useful
cannotSee.body: The schedule calls this the 07:00 Mexico City run, which would be 13:00 UTC — six hours AFTER waivers process. It actually fired at 05:41 UTC, about 65 minutes before. That is a scheduling discrepancy worth someone checking, but for today it is a gift: it is the only Wednesday brief that can still change a claim. If you are reading this after 01:00 Mexico City, the claims have already run and what matters is the free-agent half of each card.

cannotSee.body: Your claims process at 07:00 UTC. NFL teams practise Wednesday afternoon US time. Every claim here is placed on Monday and Tuesday information, and that is structural rather than a research failure — the only way to claim on a Wednesday report is to miss the window entirely.

cannotSee.label: The matchup grades are one week of opinion, not a season rank
cannotSee.body: The runbook wants each tile graded on the opponent's season rank in points allowed to that position. Two weeks in, that number does not exist. Every tile here is graded from Week 2 boards retrieved this run — Sportsnaut's for team defenses, FantasyPros' for the defense rows, Pro Football Network's for kickers — and each tile names which. Stafford's tile is marked NOT_RESEARCHED because the Giants did not appear on any board retrieved this run.

cannotSee.label: Two boards disagree about your own defense and I picked a side
cannotSee.body: FantasyPros has Jacksonville 30th; Sportsnaut has them 8th. This brief takes FantasyPros because its Jacksonville note argues forward — the five sacks came against Cleveland and are not expected to repeat — while Sportsnaut's note is a restatement of that box score. If Jacksonville finish top five at Denver, that choice was wrong and the Tampa Bay claim churned a seat for nothing.

cannotSee.label: Season projections have not moved in five snapshots
cannotSee.body: Every seasonProj figure here is identical to the ones quoted on 14 September, while weekly projections moved by up to 0.8 in the last six hours. That is the signature of a preseason artifact, not a live field. The JuiceJam trade is priced on it and fails outright when priced on this week instead — read +21.8 as August's opinion of three players.
